facts.text: On hydrostatic or electrically retarded machines, deceleration should be characterized separately for propel release, neutral request, retarder request and service brake, and for their production blend.
facts.quote: On hydrostatic or electrically retarded machines, characterize deceleration from propel release, neutral request, retarder request and service brake individually and in their production blend.

facts.text: A service-brake model that ignores hydrostatic slowing can produce early or late collision-system triggers depending on operating state.
facts.quote: A service-brake model that ignores hydrostatic slowing can produce both early and late triggers depending on operating state.

facts.text: Straight-line stopping tests should cover forward and reverse motion, several speeds, payload states, brake-temperature states, representative grades and terrain classes.
facts.quote: Forward and reverse, several speeds, payload states, brake-temperature states, representative grades and terrain classes.

facts.text: Straight-line stopping tests should measure distance from the collision-system command separately from distance from actual brake-force onset; conflating these distances hides latency.
facts.quote: Measure both distance from the collision-system command and distance from actual brake-force onset; conflating them hides latency.

facts.text: Stability testing should include braking with steering or articulation, on cross-slope and at relevant payload states, recording roll rate and angle, yaw rate, lateral acceleration, articulation angle and rate, individual wheel or track speeds and brake pressures.
facts.quote: Braking with steering or articulation, on cross-slope, at relevant payload states, recording roll rate and angle, yaw rate, lateral acceleration, articulation angle and rate, individual wheel or track speeds and brake pressures.

facts.text: ISO 3450 includes controllability requirements for certain combined brake and steer systems, making stopping distance insufficient as the sole test outcome.
facts.quote: ISO 3450 includes controllability requirements for certain combined brake and steer systems, so stopping distance is not the only outcome.

facts.text: Crawler and soft-ground identification tests should measure track speed, ground speed, slip, sinkage or rut state, and stopping response across a deliberately selected set of terrain states.
facts.quote: Track speed, ground speed, slip, sinkage or rut state and stopping response across a deliberately selected set of terrain states.

facts.text: Site-wide soil modeling is unnecessary if crawler and soft-ground tests identify a conservative envelope of available longitudinal deceleration versus state.
facts.quote: Site-wide soil modeling is unnecessary if these tests identify a conservative "available longitudinal deceleration versus state" envelope

facts.text: Detailed terramechanics is needed only where simple available-deceleration envelopes fail to transfer.
facts.quote: detailed terramechanics is needed only where simple envelopes fail to transfer.

facts.text: Brake torque depends on temperature.
facts.quote: Brake torque depends on temperature

facts.text: The historic US Bureau of Mines haul-road design manual warned that its stopping curves were primarily mathematical rather than field results.
facts.quote: the US Bureau of Mines haul-road design manual warned that its stopping curves were primarily mathematical rather than field results

facts.text: The historic US Bureau of Mines haul-road design manual warned that constant-braking calculations cannot capture heat build-up and brake fade.
facts.quote: constant-braking calculations cannot capture heat build-up and fade.

entities.name: US Bureau of Mines haul-road design manual

facts.text: Hold and restart tests should cover complete stop, brake hold, release, rollback or roll-forward on grade, and motion inhibition from standstill.
facts.quote: Complete stop, brake hold, release, rollback or roll-forward on grade, and motion inhibition from standstill.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 warns that discontinuing a collision-system intervention must not create rollaway.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3 warns that discontinuing an intervention must not create rollaway

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 recommends an operator action, such as applying the parking brake, before collision-system braking is released.
facts.quote: recommends an operator action such as applying the parking brake before collision-system braking is released.

facts.text: End-to-end latency tests should inject a known synthetic or physical object event and timestamp detection, confirmation, risk decision, brake request, machine-interface receipt, actuator response and measurable deceleration.
facts.quote: Inject a known synthetic or physical object event and timestamp detection, confirmation, risk decision, brake request, machine-interface receipt, actuator response and measurable deceleration

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 treats detection, confirmation, risk decision, brake request, machine-interface receipt, actuator response and measurable deceleration as separate portions of the collision-system distance.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3 treats these as separate portions of the collision-system distance.

facts.text: No standard or study was found that gives a required number of physical tests for calibrating a model for collision-avoidance timing.
facts.quote: No standard or study gives a required number of physical tests for calibrating a model for collision-avoidance timing: not found.

facts.text: Neither ISO 3450, ISO 10265 nor public collision-avoidance literature provides a defensible number of calibration stops guaranteeing prediction across 100-plus site types, several brake architectures and all the stated weather conditions.
facts.quote: Neither ISO 3450 nor ISO 10265 nor the public collision-avoidance literature gives a defensible number of calibration stops that guarantees prediction across 100-plus site types, several brake architectures and all the stated weather conditions

facts.text: The ISO brake standards are machine performance standards, not statistical model-transfer standards.
facts.quote: the ISO brake standards are machine performance standards, not statistical model-transfer standards.

facts.text: ISO 3450 prescribes its own brake tests, including repeated service-brake applications in the fade sequence.
facts.quote: ISO 3450 prescribes its own brake tests, for example repeated service-brake applications in the fade sequence.

facts.text: The 2026 tracked brake study used three repetitions per condition.
facts.quote: The 2026 tracked brake study used three repetitions per condition.

facts.text: Expert opinion recommends sequential design of experiments with a quantitative stop criterion, using low-risk experiments that maximally excite the parameters being estimated.
facts.quote: Use low-risk experiments that maximally excite the parameters being estimated

facts.text: Expert opinion recommends fitting the braking model to a designated calibration set, freezing its parameters, and challenging the frozen model on independent combinations not used in fitting, especially downhill, low-traction, high-payload, hot-brake and turning or cross-slope boundaries.
facts.quote: fit the model to a designated calibration set; freeze parameters; challenge the frozen model on independent combinations not used in fitting, especially downhill, low-traction, high-payload, hot-brake and turning or cross-slope boundaries

facts.text: Expert opinion recommends adding braking-model tests only where prediction intervals are too wide, residuals are systematically biased, or a case lies outside the validated domain.
facts.quote: add tests only where prediction intervals are too wide, residuals are systematically biased, or the case lies outside the validated domain.

facts.text: The proposed sequential experimental design judges test sufficiency by whether the error bound on the safety-relevant quantity is small enough at every declared operating boundary, rather than by a fixed number of tests.
facts.quote: This turns "have we run N tests?" into "is the error bound on the safety-relevant quantity small enough at every declared operating boundary?".

facts.text: Expert opinion advises never using the same stop both to tune a braking model and to claim validation.
facts.quote: Never use the same stop to both tune and claim validation

facts.text: A braking model can interpolate its calibration cases well yet fail on the first downhill or different-load condition.
facts.quote: a model can interpolate its calibration cases well and still fail on the first downhill or different-load condition.
